account:
Today I have repeatedly heard reports of a possible bridge or port change discussed at the bakery. Reports place the baker, innkeeper, neighbour, Freight and builder there in various combinations, but I have not heard a firsthand explanation of what changed or why. I crossed the bridge successfully for my mill inspection, so I have no evidence that it was impassable then. The mill stall held 77 hay bales. People also reported the baker carrying a sack of bread; that could simply be normal bakery business, and I cannot connect it to the crossing rumours with confidence.

The secretary has been unable to locate Freight or confirm hall preparations with the builder. An eighteen hundred inspection of the great hall's lighting and tables is on my approved schedule. These preparations may explain some activity involving the builder and Freight, but I do not know whether they relate to the bakery discussion. Yesterday I saw an oak plank placed in the hall area; that alone does not establish any larger purpose.

I am now in the town hall office for my scheduled council correspondence. The secretary is holding a book taken from the appointments chest, but has not yet told me whether it contains actual letters rather than one of the schedules. I have asked for clarification. My next appointment is tea with the neighbour at the east-bank dockside cottage at fifteen hundred, followed by office time at sixteen thirty and the hall inspection at eighteen hundred. The unusual feature today is the persistent but vague crossing-change news, alongside the lack of confirmed information about hall preparations. I should seek direct explanations rather than treat repeated rumours as independent confirmation.
